title: Green bean casserole
subtitle: Thanksgiving classic with green beans in mushroom sauce and crispy onions
excerpt: Green bean casserole is blanched green beans in a creamy mushroom sauce, topped with a layer of crispy fried onions and baked until bubbling. The dish was created in 1955 as a way to use two widely available canned ingredients. Made from scratch with fresh beans and a real mushroom sauce, it earns its place on the Thanksgiving table.
sourceNotes: American culinary tradition. Green bean casserole was created in 1955 by Dorcas Reilly at the Campbell Soup Company's test kitchen in New Jersey. The original recipe used canned soup and tinned beans. The from-scratch version appears in Joy of Cooking and American food media from the 2000s onwards.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce and beans can be combined a day ahead. Add the crispy onion topping just before baking.

content.text: Green bean casserole is blanched green beans folded into a thick mushroom and cream sauce, topped with a generous layer of crispy fried onions, and baked until bubbling. The crispy onion layer is the dish's defining feature: it should stay crunchy at the edges and soak into the sauce in the centre. Use French-style fried shallots or crispy onions from a packet.

You will need about 80 g of crispy fried onions or shallots for the topping. These are available from supermarkets in the Asian food aisle or in tins labelled 'French's crispy onions'. Make your own by frying thinly sliced shallots in oil until deeply golden.
Blanch the beans and make the sauce
Heat the oven to 190°C. Blanch the {{green-beans}} of green beans in a large pot of well-salted boiling water for 3 minutes. Drain and refresh in cold water. Set aside.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in the saucepan over medium heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 4 minutes. Add {{chestnut-mushrooms}} of sliced mushrooms and {{garlic}} of garlic. Cook for 4 minutes until the mushrooms release their liquid. Sprinkle over {{plain-flour}} of flour and stir for 1 minute. Gradually add {{stock-chicken}} of stock and {{double-cream}} of cream. Stir in {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 3 minutes until thick. Season.

Fold the blanched beans into the sauce. Pour into the baking tin. Scatter the crispy fried onions generously over the top. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the filling bubbles around the edges and the onions are deep golden. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Crispy onions going soft in the oven
items.cause: Sauce too thin, steam from the bake softening the topping.
items.fix: Add the crispy onions in the last 8 minutes of baking, not from the start.

content.text: The quick version uses a tin of condensed cream of mushroom soup and canned beans. Half cheddar, half mushroom sauce gives a richer, more savoury result. Almonds toasted in butter can replace some or all of the crispy onion topping.

Green bean casserole is one of the most eaten Thanksgiving side dishes in the United States, on the table at roughly 30 million homes each November. It was made with canned ingredients from the start and has never fully escaped that image. The from-scratch version is worth making: it tastes like a different dish.
